__doc__: sim-robust-vram-headroom-v1 bounded GPU proof fragment. MERGE the 'vram_headroom' block into a full-chain mission runtime-config (the live_pose capstone, e.g. mission-runtime-coldlive.json). It turns on the opt-in VRAM headroom monitor: it samples USED VRAM on the SIM clock every sample_period_s (0.2 s, sub-second so a transient spike between the orchestrator's 20 s samples is still seen), and when FREE VRAM drops below floor_mib it SHEDS optional load in a fixed named order, logging each shed by name with the reading, and names the 12 GiB ceiling by name if it is reached anyway. Absent (or {"enabled": false}) => no monitor is constructed => byte-identical. The crash-safe recording (mission-progress.jsonl + the out-of-process finalizer in run_mobile_restock.sh) is ALWAYS on and needs no config -- it only adds a sidecar, so the success-path mission.json is byte-identical. GPU rule: one run at a time via flock /tmp/aile-gpu.lock, never --force, whispr never touched.
_shed_order_note: capture_rate = widen the walkthrough record stride (a recording, never an honest-stage input). arm_feed_economy = cap the eye-in-hand masked-depth publish rate -- STAGE-BLOCKED in collect/transfer/verify (nvblox needs the feed there) AND it has no safe runtime actuator today, so the monitor skips it and escalates (set masked_depth.economy at boot instead; see masked-depth-economy-mission-fragment.json). secondary_cameras = DESTROY the station decode render products this run never reads (the fm380/fm381 teardown, ~0.95 GB+ returned, keep_shelf_camera protects a camera a later stage still reads). The monitor NEVER sheds the live_pose transfer arm feed, nvblox, or the planner.
_run_A: FULL CAPSTONE with the monitor ON. Command: the usual capstone241 live_pose cold run (fresh commission, no injection) with this block merged. PASS = mission.json state=complete AND (free VRAM never dropped below floor_mib) OR (every shed below the floor was logged by name: grep VRAM_SHED / VRAM_CEILING_REACHED in the console + host-stack.log). Record the peak: vram-headroom.json carries peak_used_mib + the fired_sheds list + ceiling_reached. Expect the completes' ~11.7 GB peak either stays above the 800 MiB floor (quiet monitor) or triggers capture_rate/secondary_cameras sheds that pull it back -- either is a PASS as long as the run completes and every shed is named.
_run_B: STAGED TRANSFER with the monitor ON, Isaac deliberately killed mid-stage with SIGSEGV. Command: a start_at=transfer staged run (recorded_bay_park staging) with this block merged; once the transfer stage is underway, `kill -SIGSEGV <isaac mission python pid>` (the pid printed as host_stack_pid's sibling -- the run_mobile_restock.py process, NOT the host stack, NOT whispr). PASS = the run dir ends with mission.json present, state=crashed, crash_signal=11 (SIGSEGV), last_stage=transfer, a stage_ladder with the completed prefix, and last_vram from vram-headroom.json; the finalizer line 'FINALIZE_CRASH wrote .../mission.json: state=crashed ...' appears from run_mobile_restock.sh (the surviving shell parent); the GPU lock is released and whispr untouched. The record-first teardown / check_walkthrough_run.py then run on the crashed record.
_expected_pass: Run A: state=complete + VRAM never below floor OR every shed named + peak recorded. Run B: mission.json state=crashed + crash_signal=11 + the stage ladder + last_vram, teardown clean.

_suggested_env.RESTOCK_RENDER_WIDTH: 960 (unchanged -- render resolution is NOT the VRAM lever, memory mission-vram-ceiling-12gb)
_suggested_env.RESTOCK_DROP_UNUSED_SENSING: optional -- drops the never-read shelf camera (~0.95 GB) pre-boot; the monitor's secondary_cameras shed does the same under pressure
